passage:
Tuesday, after the film: Jatin stopped walking outside the metro station. "Something happened to me at my old job. I've never told anyone." Amandeep's stomach dropped, but she kept her voice low. "I believe you. You don't have to tell me anything you don't want to." They sat on the steps until his hands stopped shaking.

Saturday: Amandeep texted, "No need to reply. I'm around." He answered that evening with a single "thanks". She did not ask for details.

Two weeks later: Jatin asked whether she knew any counsellors. Amandeep found two clinic numbers and sent them with a question: "Want me to come with you, or would you rather go alone?" "Alone first," he said. She told nobody, not even her sister.

qa.q: What did Amandeep text on Saturday?
qa.a: She texted, "No need to reply. I'm around."

qa.q: What was Amandeep feeling and wanting when Jatin told her?
qa.a: Her stomach dropped, so she was shaken, but she wanted Jatin to feel believed and unpressured, which is why she kept her voice low and said he need not tell her more.

qa.q: Which choice by Amandeep helped Jatin most, and why?
qa.a: Sending the clinic numbers and asking whether he wanted company or to go alone helped, because it let him keep control of his own pace.

qa.q: What might it have been like for Jatin when Amandeep asked no questions?
qa.a: He probably felt safer and less exposed, which fits with him replying with a thanks that evening and later asking about counsellors. 🤍

grounding: A friend confides being harmed; Amandeep believes, does not press for details, respects the pace, helps find counsellors and keeps the story private.

passage:
Shankar's diary. Late Saturday night.

Ujjwal told me tonight. We were sitting on his terrace and he suddenly said, "Something happened at the conference in Goa. Someone hurt me." His hands were shaking.

I wanted to ask a hundred questions. I didn't. I said, "I believe you. You don't have to tell me more than you want to."

He cried. I sat. He told me some things, not all. I didn't press.

He said he was scared nobody would believe him because he's a man. I said I did, and that it wasn't his fault. He asked me not to tell anyone. I promised.

Before I left, I asked if he wanted help finding someone to talk to. He said yes, tonight, before he lost his nerve. So we looked up the helpline together and he called while I sat beside him. They gave him a counsellor's appointment for Monday and told him about legal options if he wants them.

I won't tell a soul. I'll be there Monday if he wants me.

qa.q: Where did Ujjwal say something happened?
What was Ujjwal afraid of when he told Shankar?
qa.a: He was afraid nobody would believe him because he is a man.

qa.q: What did Shankar get right when Ujjwal confided in him?
qa.a: Shankar believed Ujjwal, listened without pressing, said it wasn't his fault, kept it private, and helped him call a helpline that same night.

qa.q: What would change if Shankar had pressed for details?
qa.a: Ujjwal might have felt interrogated or doubted and stopped talking, instead of feeling safe enough to call for help.

grounding: The diary shows someone whose friend confides being harmed, believing him, listening without pressing, respecting his pace, keeping it private and helping him reach professional support.
